business_problem: DMI's aging multi-vendor storage environment could not keep up with rapidly growing weather and climate datasets, consumed too much energy, and made it harder to provide low-cost access while preparing for hybrid-cloud scale.
solution_summary: During a Copenhagen data-center move, the Danish Meteorological Institute replaced its fragmented storage estate with a unified IBM architecture centered on IBM Storage Scale. The platform became the shared file and control layer across flash, disk, tape, and cloud tiers so climate scientists and operational teams could reach data through one interface instead of multiple siloed systems. IBM Storage Archive handles long-term retention on tape for colder datasets, while IBM Storage Protect moves data to tape and recalls it when users request it. IBM also structured the migration in two phases so data could move out of the old tape library, the new system could be relocated into the new facility, and user access could continue. The result is a more sustainable, lower-cost storage foundation that supports forecasting, climate research, and future hybrid-cloud and machine-learning work.

solution_components.name: IBM Storage Scale
solution_components.role: Provides the unified file-storage layer spanning flash, disk, tape, and cloud for DMI's weather and climate datasets.

solution_components.name: IBM Storage Archive
solution_components.role: Stores long-term archived meteorological data on tape to reduce energy use and retention cost.

solution_components.name: IBM Storage Protect
solution_components.role: Moves data to tape and retrieves it on demand so archived datasets remain accessible through the unified environment.

data_flow: Weather-station and satellite data lands in the unified Storage Scale environment, colder historical data is tiered to tape through Storage Archive and Storage Protect, and researchers and operational users access all tiers through one interface while downstream forecasting workloads consume the same managed data estate.
business_outcome: DMI gained a single scalable storage platform for operational forecasting and climate research, reduced storage cost and energy intensity, and made long-term weather data easier to retain and serve to scientists and public users.
architecture_clues: The new estate combines flash, spinning disk, tape, and cloud in one storage system.
DMI stores much of its data in Copenhagen while forecasting calculations run on a supercomputer in Iceland.
IBM executed the migration in two parts so the storage system could move between old and new data-center locations without cutting off access.
evidence_quotes: Our storage system was getting too old to cope with future demands.
IBM Storage Scale ... has the capacity to combine flash, disk, tape and cloud storage into a unified system.
IBM Storage Archive stores archived data on tape and IBM Storage Protect moves the data to tape and retrieves it when a user requests it.
The entire process is transparent to the end users, who access all data, regardless of where it resides, from a single interface.
There has been a reduction in the cost per petabyte of data that is stored on tape in the new system compared to the old system.
